subject: ela
intro: Eighth graders analyze how a text makes connections among and distinctions between individuals, ideas, or events, through comparisons, analogies, or categories. Authors group and contrast ideas to help readers understand: comparing two leaders, analogizing a system to a machine, or sorting information into categories.

items.prompt:
Read.

Like a thermostat, the body senses when it is too hot and triggers sweating to cool down.

What kind of connection is the author making?

steps: Comparing the body to a thermostat to explain it is an analogy.
So the author uses an analogy to explain how the body regulates temperature.
solution.answer: An analogy (body is like a thermostat) to explain temperature regulation.

items.prompt:
Read.

The text sorts energy sources into two groups: renewable (solar, wind) and nonrenewable (coal, oil).

What method does the author use to organize ideas?

steps: Grouping into renewable vs nonrenewable is using categories.
So the author organizes by categories.

items.prompt:
Read.

Unlike the first president, who avoided parties, the second openly took sides.

What distinction is drawn?

steps: The text contrasts the two presidents' attitudes toward parties.
So it draws a distinction (contrast) between the two leaders.
solution.answer: A contrast between the two presidents' attitudes toward parties.

items.prompt: Comparing two things to explain one is an ____.
Showing how two things differ is a ____.
